stem: You declare a variable `env` in `variables.tf` with `default = "dev"`. You also have `env = "staging"` in `terraform.tfvars`, and you run `terraform apply -var="env=prod"`. Which value does Terraform use?
options: "staging" — values from .tfvars files take highest precedence
Terraform errors because the variable is assigned in more than one place
"prod" — the -var flag takes highest precedence over both .tfvars and default
"dev" — the default is always the source of truth
objective: Choose between -var flag, .tfvars file, and TF_VAR_ environment variable to supply a value, explaining the precedence order

stem: A colleague sets `export TF_VAR_bucket_name=corp-assets` in their shell but forgot to declare a `bucket_name` variable block in the configuration. What does Terraform do?
options: Prints a warning about the undeclared variable, the same as a .tfvars file would
Creates the variable automatically from the environment variable
Raises an error and refuses to continue, the same as -var would
Silently ignores the environment variable and continues
objective: Choose between -var flag, .tfvars file, and TF_VAR_ environment variable to supply a value, explaining the precedence order

stem: You want the `aws_s3_bucket` resource to use the value of an input variable called `bucket_name`. Which resource argument is correct?
objective: Declare input variables with type, description, default, and validation, then reference them inside resource arguments using var.<NAME>
